To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a subgroup of HPV-negative/relapse-associated VSCC by a combined proteomic and immunohistochemical analysis.

we could identify a subgroup of VSCC tumors that are HPV negative and associated with relapse, that this subgroup is characterized by altered interferon response, and that the ubiquitin-protein pathway is also altered in this subgroup.
we have developed and validated a new approach to tumor proteomics that can be used for characterization of tumor phenotypes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of biomarkers that can aid the clinical diagnosis of VSCC.
the development of a novel method for analysis of tumor proteomes.
the identification and characterization of VSCC subtypes, which is of clinical relevance since relapse risk is associated with the HPV negative subgroup.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our data suggest that HPV negative tumors have a different biology and that the high risk HPV-negative/relapse-associated group is characterized by altered interferon signaling, and that these tumors may be associated with a more aggressive disease course.

HPV positive tumors are characterized by low levels of interferon-regulated proteins, whereas HPV negative tumors are characterized by high levels of interferon regulated proteins, and that this is associated with a high risk of relapse in HPV negative tumors.
HPV negative tumors with relapse have altered interferon signaling and ubiquitin-protease pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HPV negative tumors with relapse risk have a different tumor proteome and a different biological profile compared to tumors with HPV infection and/or no relapse risk.
the combination of proteome-wide protein quantification, pathway analysis and multivariate statistical analysis of the data can provide new information on tumor subtypes.
the proposed approach of tumor proteome analysis is valuable for characterization of cancer subtypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed method can be used for identification of protein biomarkers for HPV and relapsed VSCC.
pathway fingerprinting can be used for identification of protein markers and for identification of biological processes associated with disease.
the proposed method can be used to identify tumor subgroups and to provide a biological rationale for the subgroup differences.
